newsitem.title: CANADA: B.C. premier says balanced budget vow 'challenged'.
newsitem.headline: B.C. premier says balanced budget vow 'challenged'.

text.p: British Columbia Premier Glen Clark said Monday his government was facing a challenge in keeping its promise of a balanced budget this year.
Speaking to reporters, Clark listed the government's many campaign promises with the balanced budget the last among them. "The only one that is challenged is the latter," he said.
The Vancouver Sun newspaper reported that Clark said Saturday he did not know if he could still deliver a surplus this year.
The NDP government in a budget announced before a May election, which it won by a narrow margin, forecast a C$87 million surplus in 1996/97.

According to the Sun, Clark was asked Saturday if he can still deliver a surplus this year. "Don't know. It's too early to say. Spending is not the problem -- we're not overspending -- the problem is the revenue forecasts. "
"I guess it depends on how dramatic the revenue drop is, whether it is prudent or desirable to cut that much if the revenue drops off precipitously," he was quoted as saying.

"Under normal circumstances -- what's been normal for the last five years -- if we have a revenue drop of C$200 million or C$300 million then clearly we can cut that amount to balance the budget...If there is a spectacular drop in revenue then that becomes a big challenge because you can't adjust fast enough," Clark said.

He declined to be drawn on the subject when speaking with reporters at the provincial legislature Monday. The government aims to make C$750 million in spending cuts and take C$400 million from a forest industry renewal fund to bolster its finances in the face of lower than expected revenues.
